name: Chervil
grown_as: An annual herb sown for its delicate aniseed-flavoured leaves, best in cool weather and light shade
habit: A soft, lacy, bright green plant 30 to 60 cm tall, much branched. Stem slender, finely grooved, hairy just above the nodes.

leaf.arrangement: Lower leaves in a loose rosette; stem leaves alternate
leaf.type: Compound, two or three times pinnate, fern-like
leaf.leaflets: Small, deeply cut into narrow lobes with blunt-pointed tips
leaf.outline: Triangular, 5 to 15 cm long, flat and lacy
leaf.margin: Deeply cut into lobes and a few teeth all round each leaflet
leaf.surface: Soft and thin, finely downy beneath
leaf.stalk: Lower leaves on long stalks with a sheathing base; upper leaves on the sheath alone
leaf.colour: Bright fresh pale green, often turning purplish in cold or drought

flower.form: Small loose umbels of tiny flowers
flower.petals: Five tiny white petals per flower, a little unequal
flower.behind: No bracts; two to five small bracteoles on one side under each small umbel, turned down
flower.carried: Opposite the leaves, on very short stalks or none, with 3 to 6 downy rays
flower.size: Umbels 2 to 4 cm; flowers about 2 mm

fruit: Long narrow seeds 7 to 10 mm in pairs, smooth, with a short beak at the tip; green then dark brown to black
seedling: Two long narrow seed leaves, then a first true leaf already lacy
winter: Nothing in most gardens: an annual, though autumn sowings can survive a mild winter as small plants

leaf: fern-like leaf divided two or three times
small leaflets deeply cut into blunt lobes
bloom: short or no stalk under the umbel
seed: long narrow smooth seed with a short beak
young: a small rosette of lacy bright green leaves
crop: a soft lacy clump of fern-like leaves, no flowers
flower: small white umbels sitting close to the leaves
seedhead: long narrow beaked seeds in pairs

look_alikes: Cow parsley (Anthriscus sylvestris) is a taller perennial with umbels on long stalks and darker leaves. Fool's parsley (Aethusa cynapium, poisonous) has long hanging bracteoles and an unpleasant smell. Hemlock has purple-blotched stems. Its own aniseed smell is the best test.
